actions: Searched public sources for persistent self-improving systems exposing multiple controller actions including stop/restart/widen/reopen.
Audited FORGE paper protocol and matched/no-graduation ablations.
Audited public FORGE implementation at main SHA 6d3f46a3dca2ec20574d77185a19d01062005177, including frozen stage evaluation, post-session evaluation and crash-resume path.
Identified that public resume does not persist/reconstruct graduated_instances, so restart can reactivate/overwrite previously frozen solutions.
Persisted a source-bound controller-action matrix and sequence-73 checkpoint; advanced LATEST and verified readback.
material_findings: FORGE places Continue, Restart-with-artifact, Widen, champion broadcast/resume-best and Stop/Freeze in one persistent self-improvement protocol.

FORGE vs isolated Reflexion provides same-system evidence for population broadcast; no-graduation shows stopping mainly saves compute but can prematurely terminate learning and hurt final performance.
FORGE uses frozen selection checkpoints and separate post-session frozen evaluations, but not a physically isolated outer benchmark split.

Current public crash-resume code loses prior graduation controller state even though artifacts survive, demonstrating that durable self-improvement requires controller-state reconciliation in addition to artifact persistence.
termination_cause: runtime turn completion after substantive checkpoint; frontier remains nonempty
exact_next_action: Search for a persistent self-improving agent that directly compares at least three of Stop / Continue / Restart-clean / Restart-with-artifact / Widen / Resume-ancestor / Reopen under matched total proposal/evaluation budget and a selection-unused outer test. Prefer explicit crash-resume tests preserving frozen/retired controller state; separately audit anytime-valid promotion, cross-proposal durable statistical spending, immutable identity, feedback bandwidth and complete proposal chronology.
